In this case, we have an indeterminate form of type $\frac{\infty }{\infty },$ so applying L'Hopital's rule yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[{x}^{3}]^{′}}{[{ln}^{2}⁡x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{3{x}^{2}}{(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{3{x}^{3}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[3{x}^{3}]^{′}}{{[2\operatorname{ln}⁡x]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{9{x}^{2}}{(\frac{2}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{9{x}^{3}}{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
